prose_updates.tldr: Branch-sCIDP is a finite sound formula search over the published positive discrete selected-COPAG class, with pointwise terminal soundness conditioned on the continuous-version choices required by Chen--Mooij's Theorem 4.14(3). The reusable selection-equalizer lift constructs denominator-locked selected witnesses from suitable observationally equivalent base SCMs. Separately, the affine compiler is a conditional one-table observational-fiber rank test: for a supplied represented family with an explicit reachable role trace, it simultaneously preserves the normalized selected observational law and the positive conditioning denominator while extracting a rational pair with different joint numerators. The implication from all-branch failure to such a represented locked construction, and therefore the advertised formula-or-certificate complexity theorem, remains open.

project_justification.gap: Failure of a selected terminal joint-identification call does not by itself preserve its conditioning denominator. The published pointwise soundness result also requires continuous versions at Rule L2 applications and does not prove selected conditional completeness, leaving the residual-forest-to-lock implication unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The paper separates a sound reachable-role formula search from two constructive nonidentification tools: a reusable selection-equalizer lift and a conditional exact rank compiler on a supplied one-table observational fiber. The graph-to-lock implication connecting universal branch failure to either tool is retained as an open question.
project_justification.fill: The precise affine addition is simultaneous exact preservation of the complete normalized selected observational law and the terminal conditioning denominator, separation of the terminal joint numerator, and extraction of an explicit positive rational certificate. Its transfer to the original query uses the affine family's displayed legal role trace. The equalizer lift supplies an independent reusable construction, while no general formula-or-certificate synthesis theorem is claimed.

prose_updates.related_work: Chen and Mooij provide the selected-COPAG model and pointwise \(\operatorname{sIDP}\) soundness under the continuous-version hypothesis in Theorem 4.14(3), with Remark 4.4(2) covering the positive discrete subclass. Their results motivate the role search and residual-forest question but do not supply denominator-locked selected conditional completeness. Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim's Algorithm 2 supplies the no-selection CIDP bucket-intersection transitions and normalization, and their Theorem 4 supplies completeness; the present regression claim is limited to equality of identification decisions. Abouei and coauthors address an unconditional selected intervention target in a known augmented graph. Shpitser and Pearl give the fixed-graph conditional benchmark, and Duarte and coauthors motivate exact finite discrete fiber computation. Against this background, the equalizer lift is used as a reusable construction lemma, whereas the affine compiler is a conditional exact rank test for simultaneous observational-law and denominator preservation on a supplied one-table family, with rational certificate extraction.
prose_updates.honest_scope: No selected conditional completeness theorem is claimed. Pointwise use of \(\operatorname{sIDP}\) is restricted to runs choosing continuous versions at every Rule L2 application. The no-selection comparison asserts equality of identification decisions only; it neither asserts equality of returned functionals nor imports an unattested CIDP soundness theorem. The affine rank equivalence applies to a supplied rational interior one-table family that includes a reachable terminal state, a displayed legal trace, inherited assignments, represented graph coordinates, forests for the entire terminal intervention, and an interval remaining in the represented model class. The compiler's guarantee is simultaneous exact preservation of the normalized selected observational law and the positive conditioning denominator with separation of the numerator and rational certificate extraction. The generic equalizer lift produces a positive rational finite witness in the published discrete class and is binary only when all endogenous and latent base variables are binary; the explicit table and affine certificates are binary. An isolated conditioning root makes denominator equality vacuous, so the deleted bow baseline is not evidence for graph-to-lock. Universal all-branch failure has not been shown to yield a passing represented family, and no \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\Gamma})\) formula-or-certificate synthesis theorem is asserted. Continuous variables, intervention inputs, faithfulness-only conclusions, and general finite-alphabet certificate completeness remain outside scope.
